question: Codex Selden / Codex Añute
answer: The Codex Selden is a very detailed piece of writing; it is meant to be read in a certain order, gives names, status, locations, time, actions, etc. and it can all be understood as a cohesive storyline. It doesn’t have a single written word but they give immense amounts of detail that give us insight into the values of the pre-colonial city-states.

question: History of the Codex
answer: The Codex Selden carries its name after scholar John Selden who possessed the document and made sure it would be donated to the University of Oxford upon his death.

question: Codex Mendoza & Speech
answer: The Codex Mendoza challenges contemporary understandings of not only writing, but also specifically the relationship between writing and speech.

question: A Collaborative Effort
answer: This encyclopedia was a collaborative effort between Sahagún and Nahua scholars to document indigenous knowledge during a period of conquest, disease, and colonial restrictions that ultimately shaped the content. Pictured is an example of what a page in the encyclopedia looked like, made up of Nahua paintings, Nahua descriptions, and Spanish translations of Nahua content.

question: Notice the Prologues
answer: They are written strictly in Spanish by Sahagún to frame the project through his perspective and for the anticipated Christian audience for conversion.

question: Notice the Spanish text
answer: The Spanish translations act as a shorter, secondary interpretation of the detailed Nahua accounts, often summarizing or omitting the content as a political tool in creating tension and undermining the preservation of Nahua culture.

question: Notice the Nahuatl descriptions
answer: The detailed and expressive Nahua text served not only to document their history and culture, but also to preserve and keep their cultural traditions alive for future Nahua audiences. Although they had adopted Hispanic values and religion, writing was used as a tool for processing their own livelihoods and traditions.

question: Notice the Images
answer: The Nahua paintings combine European and Indigenous artistic traditions to preserve Nahua culture while working alongside the text to communicate a fuller story through visual representation.
